newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: SOCCER-SUBSTITUTE HITS TWO AS SAUDI ARABIA ENTER SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SUBSTITUTE HITS TWO AS SAUDI ARABIA ENTER SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Substitute Yousif Al Thunai scored twice as Saudi Arabia came back from two goals down to beat China 4-3 on Monday and clinch an Asian Cup semifinal berth.
Striker Sami Jaber and Fahad Mahalel added the other two goals to put Saudi Arabia through for a Wednesday showdown against Iran -- who earlier stunned South Korea with a 6-2 thrashing.
Hosts the United Arab Emirates face Kuwait in the second semifinal.
China took only six minutes to go into the lead with defender Zhang Enhua rising unchallenged to head in a corner from the right.
The Chinese continued to look dangerous and might have snatched a second in the 15th minute but for an acrobatic save by Saudi Keeper Mohammed Al Daeyea from a volley by Xie Hui.
Peng Weiguo gave China a deserved second goal a minute later, sliding in to divert a low drive across the goal into the net.
The turning point came in the 30th minute when the Saudis made a tactical change, taking off a defender and putting on winger Thunai. It paid off immediately.
Less than 60 seconds after coming on, Thunai tapped in a loose ball from a tight angle after China's keeper Ou Chuliang had made a fine save to put Saudi Arabia back in the match.
Three minutes later the Saudis levelled the scores, Jaber turning in a low cross by Mahalel from a tight angle.
Saudi Arabia took command from then on and Mahalel put them 3-2 ahead in the 43rd minute before Thunai put the tie beyond doubt with his second in the 65th minute.
Zhang scored his second and his team's third a minute before the final whistle but it was too late for the Chinese.

China: 20-Ou Chuliang; 4-Zhang Enhua; 5-Xu Hong; 6-Fan Zhiyi; 8-Ma Mingyu (9-Cao Xiandong 52); 11-Peng Weiguo (7-Hao Haidong 57); 13-Sun Jihai; 14-Jiang Feng; 17-Gao Feng; 21-Liu Yue (19-Wu Chengying 64); 23 Xie Hui

Saudi Arabia: 1-Mohammed Al Daeyea; 2-Mohammed Al Jahani (15-Yousif Al Thunai 30); 3-Mohammed Al Khilaiwi; 4-Abdullah Zubrom; 8-Khalid Al Temawi; 9-Sami Al Jaber; 10-Fahad Mahalel (17-Abdulla Al Garni 83); 12-Ibrahim Al Harbi (24-Khamees Al Zahrani 73); 13-Hussain Sulaimani; 14-Khalid Al Mowaled; 16- Khamis Al Dossary.
